verdict.rationale: Codex Plugins exist to let users hand tasks to the Codex/ChatGPT agent. Installed plugins add skills and tools to chats (docs-26, docs-45), such as summarizing Slack channels, drafting replies, or sending messages on the user's behalf (docs-4, docs-5). Built-in skills like @plugin-creator and the workflow recorder do the scaffolding and skill drafting for the user (docs-10, docs-15, docs-16), and a community report confirms skills can be invoked explicitly (comm-8). The assistant itself is Codex/ChatGPT rather than the plugin layer, which is why this scores 7 rather than higher. Missing for 10: hands-on evidence of delegated plugin tasks completing end-to-end, and documentation of the delegation, review and approval flow within the plugin layer.
